correctness.rationale: For \(1\le p\le2\), the Hanner sum-difference inequality applied to \(\lambda x\) and \((1-\lambda)y\) gives an upper bound on the simultaneous size of the two weighted norms; disjoint coordinate vectors attain it. For \(2\le p<\infty\), the reversed Hanner inequality applied after the change of variables \(z=\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\), \(w=\lambda x-(1-\lambda)y\) bounds the sum of the two \(p\)-th powers; a two-coordinate Hanner pair equalizes and attains the bound. The \(p=\infty\) endpoint is proved directly. The proof covers all parameters and does not infer a universal result from finite experiments.

value.rationale: The generalized James constant was introduced to quantify non-squareness, and \(\ell_p\) is the canonical test family. A complete exact formula across both parameters \(p\) and \(\lambda\) is mathematically natural, recovers the classical James constant at \(\lambda=1/2\), exposes a sharp transition at the Hilbert exponent, and identifies the extremal geometry on each side. This is a structural benchmark rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical evaluation.
